textos.f6715bca-5f9d-42b3-a57e-72504c5a7421#180: When you use the [[T0]] pass-through functions [[T1]] Function or [[T2]] Function to query data, [[T3]] returns the data to you in one or many result sets. Result sets originate from cursors in the server data source and become cursors in [[T4]]. The default name for a result set is [[T5]].

Because the server compiles each stored procedure when you create it, you receive any server syntax errors at create time. When you execute the stored procedure, the server executes the compiled [[T0]] statements sequentially (as in a [[T1]] program) and [[T2]] fetches each result set from each [[T3]] statement within the stored procedure separately, in the order executed.

Result sets and errors are returned in the order received, and processing stops if an error is encountered. For example, if a run-time error occurs when the server executes the third statement in a four-statement stored procedure, you receive the first two result sets and then receive the error that occurred upon processing the third result set. Processing stops after the error is returned; the fourth result set is not retrieved. You can use the [[T4]] Function function to obtain information about the most recent error.

> **Note:** You can execute stored procedures on a remote server from [[T5]] only by using [[T6]] [[T7]] pass-through functions. Views don't support stored procedures on a remote server, because each view contains an explicit [[T8]] statement in its [[T9]] definition.

Makes it possible for you to include a Title, Summary, or additional Detail bands in the report or label page layout and specify settings for them.

Contains options for the Title band.
 **Report has title band**
Specifies whether the layout includes a Title band for displaying information once at the beginning of the report.
**New page after title has printed**
Specifies that a page break will be sent to the printer after the Title band information has rendered. Available only when the Report has title band check box is selected.

Contains options for the Summary band.
 **Report has summary band**
Specifies whether the layout includes a Summary band for displaying information once at the end of the report.
**Summary prints as new page**
Specifies that a page break will be sent to the printer before the Summary band information is rendered. Available only when the Report has summary band check box is selected.
**Include page header with summary**
Specifies that the Page Header band information will be rendered on the separate page along with the Summary band information.
**Include page footer with summary**
Specifies that the Page Footer band information will be rendered on the separate page along with the Summary band information.

Contains options for Detail bands in the layout. The list box shows the Detail bands in the page layout and allows you to change their order, add them, or remove them.

Allows you to change the order of the Detail bands.

**Remove**
Removes the selected Detail band from the page layout. You will not be able to delete the first band in the list. The layout must contain at least on Detail band.

You can align report controls in different ways. The following list describes some of the ways you can align report controls:
 - Relative to each other.
- Relative to the grid in the designer.
- Relative to the center of the band.

- Open the report or label in the appropriate designer.
- In the designer, select the report controls you want to align.
- On the Format menu, point to Align , and click the alignment that you want. Note The Center Vertically and Center Horizontally options apply to aligning report controls relative to the band they are in. If multiple controls are selected in multiple bands, then the alignment applies to the overall layout.

When aligning report controls relative to each other, [[T0]] uses the report control whose edge is the closest to alignment you select as the anchor.

> **Tip:** Aligning horizontally placed report controls with their right side or left side cause them to overlap each other. Likewise, aligning vertically placed report controls with their top or bottom edge cause them to overlap each other. Therefore, align report controls with an edge that is open for all selected controls and away from each other.

- Open the report or label in the appropriate designer.
- On the Format menu, ensure that Snap to Grid . is selected. Any control movement you now make in the report layout will be constrained by the designer grid.

To allow future control movement to be unconstrained by the designer grid, clear the Snap to Grid setting on the Format menu.

- Open the report or label in the appropriate designer.
- In the designer, select the report controls you want to align.
- On the Format menu, point to Align , and click Center Vertically or Center Horizontally . The report controls move to the vertical or horizontal center of the band that contains them.

- How to: Adjust Report Control Position
